gen-mystery-quest-gf-saira: Mystery Quest has curves that stay open at the jaws, giving its headings a bookish, old-fashioned lilt. Saira then does the quieter job, with rounded letters stretching tall and an s you can see straight through.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-sarpanch: Storybook charm, trimmed short. Mystery Quest sets a nostalgic tone with its open-jawed curves, while Sarpanch, a sans-serif, keeps its lowercase e clearly open and its ascenders tucked close to the x-height.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Schibsted Grotesk is a sans-serif with big, open-looking e and a shapes, and terminals that never close in on themselves. Mystery Quest supplies the nostalgic, bookish flavor.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-sen: Open jaws on every curved stroke give Mystery Quest its bookish, nostalgic face, with compact ascenders over tall lowercase. Sen, a sans-serif, runs one constant line through each letter, so its curves look like bent tubing.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-sintony: Old storybook headings, meet a modern text face. Mystery Quest leans on open-jawed curves and compact ascenders; Sintony, a sans-serif, has a chunky, tall midzone and curves that stay smooth, so bump its size up a touch.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Dark, a bit snarling, and spaced wide. Eater keeps its hairlines present but not razor thin, and Noto Sans Syriac softens the mood with tall, bulb-like bowls and easy turns in its s shapes.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nagri: Flavors draws every stroke at one thickness, diagonals included, under a towering x-height that feels whimsical and bossy at once. Its pull is sheer attitude.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-tamil-sup: Round forms like open parentheses and a middle band so tall the line looks stocky: that is Noto Sans Tamil Supplement. Autour One, by contrast, is bold and expressive, with strokes as constant as bent wire and a minimal step from capitals to lowercase.
gen-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Futuristic and tile-like, Audiowide sets wide-spaced glyphs with no thick-thin shift. Noto Sans Kaithi, a sans-serif, fills the line with tall lowercase and open e channels, so a long page would read smoothly.
gen-almendra-display-fs-public-sans: Ornate and literary, Almendra Display has letters that never seem to pinch shut and a pronounced x-height. But Public Sans, a plain sans, has a hefty lowercase with broad counters, so a long passage would read steadily.
